title: Camp 2 close
hook: Krishna takes the reins; the stories you now carry
tomorrow: Janmashtami: the night Krishna was born

segments.voice: Yesterday: the eve. The conches sounded, and Arjuna's bow slipped from his hand. The night before.

Before the war, before the conches, there's a scene the Mahabharata tells almost like a joke. Arjuna and Duryodhana both go to Krishna to ask for his help in the coming war. Krishna is asleep. Duryodhana arrives first and sits proudly by his head. Arjuna comes in and sits quietly at his feet. Krishna wakes, and the first person he sees is Arjuna. So he makes an offer. On one side, my whole army, a vast force of warriors. On the other, me, alone, and I won't lift a weapon in the war. Choose.
screen: `TWO COUSINS AT KRISHNA'S BED.` → `ONE AT HIS HEAD, ONE AT HIS FEET.` → `MY ARMY, OR ME, UNARMED.`

segments.voice: Arjuna, asked first, chooses Krishna. No army, just him. Duryodhana can hardly believe his luck: he gets the army. Then Arjuna asks Krishna for one thing: drive my chariot. So the one the Gita will reveal as God becomes a driver, a sarathi, the one who holds the reins. Krishna is still called Parthasarathi, the charioteer of Arjuna, and there are temples to him by that name. That's where Camp 2 ends: a frightened man in a chariot, and the one holding the reins about to speak. Now look back at what you're carrying. Fifty-five stories. A boy made from earth guarding a door, and an elephant head. The broken tusk that finished the Mahabharata. A mouse carrying a god: vahana. A sweet that comes back to you: prasad. A baby grabbing at the sun, a leap across the sea, a burning tail, a mountain carried whole: sankat mochan. A king with no sons, a bow, fourteen years, sandals on a throne, the forest years: vanaprastha. A golden deer. Lakshmana rekha. An old bird who tried. Shabari's berries. A squirrel on Rama Setu. A foot nobody could lift. Ten heads, a hymn to the sun, a queen's grief. Agni pariksha, the scene i didn't tidy up. Diwali, the lamps. Then cousins, dice, a cloth that wouldn't end, five villages, and the eve. When someone mentions Hanuman now, or Draupadi, or Bharata's sandals, you won't nod politely. You'll know. You know these people now. Next come the practices, the things these stories were pointing at all along. And when a festival's date arrives, its story comes first.
screen: `ARJUNA CHOOSES KRISHNA, UNARMED.` · `SARATHI: THE ONE WHO HOLDS THE REINS.` · `FIFTY-FIVE STORIES YOU CARRY.` · `YOU KNOW THESE PEOPLE NOW.`

segments.voice: Picture a chariot, and someone steady holding the reins, then let the faces walk past one at a time, like a crowded station: Ganesha, Hanuman, Sita, Lakshmana, Jatayu, Shabari, Vibhishana, Mandodari, Draupadi, Arjuna. Don't try to remember everything; just notice which face stops and looks at you. That's the one you're carrying out of this camp.
The driver. Sarathi, the one who holds the reins: Krishna, choosing to drive Arjuna's chariot instead of fighting.
Your line: you know these people now. That's Camp 2, all fifty-five stories. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus also call Krishna Parthasarathi, Arjuna's charioteer, and the image of Krishna holding the reins while Arjuna listens is a familiar one in Hindu homes, in temples and on the covers of the Bhagavad Gita.
